Remove noisy/useless print around model.summary() call

In the TensorflowModel constructor, model.summary() is called to output
a summary of the model created/loaded. TF's summary() prints itself, but
returns None, so the print() around it always prints "None".

OCR-D just configured the amount of noi... console output wanted
from TensorFlow, so while I don't get any output from summary() anymore,
I do see this spurious "None", which we didn't notice before within the
other messages by TF.

Only applies to Calamari 1.0, I think - but I didn't check 2.x very
thoroughly.

API docs:
https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/Model#summary

Re-implement early termination using jthread

Previously, Peregrine used pthread_cancel() to implement early
termination. This was a bit of an unstructured disaster and required
care throughout the remaining codebase. C++20 has jthreads, which can be
requested to stop by any thread, and zero-cost exceptions, so this
commit uses jthreads along with a barebones custom exception to achieve
the same results in a cleaner manner.

Along with this change, the thread local values are no longer stored in
a thread-local space, but managed on the heap by the aggregator. This
means that on worker exit we don't lose aggregation values, so there is
no need to synchronize worker exits with aggregator access.

Finally, this does mean that g++-9 is no longer supported, as jthreads
were implemented as of libstdc++ 10.1. See more here:
https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/status.html#status.iso.2020

Refactor partial order generation code.

Use a simpler implementation that follows the symmetry breaking paper
exactly, except that instead of using the largest eclass, you use the
first one. Since the patterns are sorted by degree and neighbour degree,
the earlier eclasses will contain vertices that comprise the pattern
core. If conditions are first placed on core vertices, you won't have
conditions spanning sibling groups.

Additionally, we need to handle the case that an order group straddles a
core vertex. This only happens in patterns with anti-edges. E.g.
[1-2][1-3][1-4](2~3)(3~4), where 2 < 3 < 4 and there is only one sibling
group. This is a problem because 2's lower bound is 4's upper bound, but
they're in the same order group. This leads to no matches being found. To
deal with this, we need to split up the order group that normally
occurs, e.g. {2, 4}, into two, and tell the matcher not to find an upper
bound for the sibling group when computing its candidate set.

Parallel match output to disk

Implement match output natively for user convenience.

For now, CSV and packed binary output formats are available. New formats
can be easily added by putting another `else if constexpr` block in
`OutputManager::output`.

There are two recommended ways of using the disk output module:

* `output<OutputFormat>(data_graph, patterns, nworkers)`
  This will write every match for each `p` in `patterns` to files
  `./{p.to_string()}/{0..nworkers-1}`.

* `output<...>(data_graph, patterns, nworkers, process)`
  This takes the same template parameters and arguments as `match(...)`
  and lets you call `a.template output<OutputFormat>(cm.mapping)` in
  your process function to write matches to the same locations as above.
  So you can easily modify existing code which calls `match()` in order
  to output matches.

Both functions return a vector of 3-tuples: one per input pattern. The
tuples consist of (pattern, aggregation value, path to output).

By default the per-pattern directories are created at the current
directory, but both functions have an optional final argument to change
this. For example you can write:
  `auto res = output<BIN>(data_graph, patterns, nworkers, "./out/");`

The sample application in `apps/output.cc` shows basic usage. Compile it
with `make output`.

bug in treetops ID check

There was a bug on treetop ID.
However, it raises a question about the expected third column, which seems to be an ID and not a Z value as it is given by tree_detection. Thus if several tree tops have the exact same height, the algorithm throws an error. And if several tops have the same integer part they will be identified with the same color. Thus
Thus, to make it work properly without the user-defined ID option (like in the other algorithms):
- I replaced treetops_df[, 3] by  treetops_df[[3]]
- I changed to generate a unique treetops_df integer ID systematically
If the possibility to have a user-defined treetop ID is wanted, it could be either given in a new argument or expressed specifically to be the third column or the RasterLayer value in the manual. In that case, this option should be thought for the other algorithms as well, to be homogeneous and to keep lastrees working, shouldn't it?

optimization debian package manager tweaks

By default, Ubuntu or Debian based "apt" or "apt-get" system installs recommended but not suggested packages .

By passing "--no-install-recommends" option, the user lets apt-get know not to consider recommended packages as a dependency to install.

This results in smaller downloads and installation of packages .

Refer to blog at [Ubuntu Blog](https://ubuntu.com/blog/we-reduced-our-docker-images-by-60-with-no-install-recommends) .
